problem: Which of the following diagrams gives the slope field at the points indicated for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=y-1?$
worked_solution:
We have to sketch the slope field at the points $(-2,-2),(1,1)$ and $(2,1).$

To sketch the slope field at the given points, we substitute their coordinates into the right-hand side of the differential equation.

$$
\begin{aligned} & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(-2,-2)}=-2-1=-3, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(1,1)}=1-1=0, \\  & {\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{(2,1)}=1-1=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting up our points and drawing our line segments, we get the following:
